newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bezeq offer to be delayed until November.
newsitem.headline: Bezeq offer to be delayed until November.

text.p: The Israeli government's offering of shares in state-owned Bezeq Israel Telecom will not take place in August as planned, a top economic official said on Sunday.
Moshe Leon, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's chief economic adviser, said he did not know when the offering would now take place but company sources said it would likely occur in November.
Instead, the government hopes to complete a block trade to institutional investors in August for an as yet undetermined percentage of the telecommunications company, sources said.
"The government wants to show they're moving with the privatisation," the source said.
The deadline for the public offering, which is to be for up to 10 percent of equity, was due to be filed on July 10 and completed by August 31.
"If we were going to do it in August they would have had to file a few days ago to the Securitlies Authority," a source involved in the offering told Reuters.
"It was never realistic to do it in August," the source said.

The November offering will be based on Bezeq's second-quarter results and contain domestic and European tranches, similar to offerings made in the state-owned Israel Discount Bank in April and Bank Leumi in May.

A tender open to Israel and foreign investment banks to conduct the block trade was quietly published by the Government Corporations Authority in April. Among those who submitted bids was Merrill Lynch, the source said.
In June, Merrill Lynch acquired shares for a block trade in Israel's Agis Industries Ltd, a pharmaceuticals company, for approximately $58.6 million and charged a 10 percent transaction fee.

The size of the block trade will depend on the extent of demand, the source said. If there is enough demand, the authority may decide to reduce the size of the public offering and perhaps even cancel it, he said.
"They want to keep everything open. The government wants to go both ways, although it's confusing," the source said.
Selling shares by block trade would not require publishing a prospectus, the source said, but would entail selling the shares at a discount to the market price.

All told, the authority is authorised to sell up to 24 percent of Bezeq. But analysts have said they doubt the domestic capital market could absorb even the 10 percent of Bezeq slated for the public offering without considerable foreign interest.
At Bezeq's current market capitalisation, a 10 percent offering would be worth just over $200 million.
The Bezeq offering is widely viewed as a major step forward in the effort by Netanyahu's government to speed up privatisation.

It has floated 24 percent of the company, but in 1995 Britain's Cable and Wireless PLC bought up about 10 percent of the public float on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. Further share offerings have been delayed while Cable and the government sought to determine Cables' future role at Bezeq.
